description: Fix video player on TV so controls (CC/subtitle, settings, play/pause) are accessible via D-pad remote. The embedded vaplayer.ru player works on mobile touch but on Android TV WebView the HTML controls are not clickable/visible because WebView does not translate D-pad events into mouse/touch events. Solution: Inject JavaScript into WebView that (1) listens for keydown events and shows/focuses player controls, (2) enables keyboard navigation within the embedded player, AND (3) add a native TV controls overlay with Play/Pause, Subtitle toggle, and Back buttons as TVFocusable elements that communicate with the WebView via injectJavaScript/postMessage.
steps: 1. In apps/mobile/src/components/VideoPlayer.jsx: Add a webViewRef using useRef to access the WebView instance for calling injectJavaScript().

2. In apps/mobile/src/components/VideoPlayer.jsx: Enhance the injectedJavaScript to add TV-specific keyboard/remote handling. Inject code that: (a) Listens for 'keydown' events in the WebView (Android TV D-pad sends keydown events to WebView), (b) On any key press, shows the player's built-in controls by dispatching a mouse move event or clicking the video element (which typically toggles controls in HTML5 players), (c) Maps D-pad center/Enter key to play/pause toggle, (d) Maps D-pad left/right to seek backward/forward by 10 seconds, (e) Finds subtitle/CC buttons in the player DOM and triggers them when the user presses a specific key. Post messages back to React Native about player state.

3. In apps/mobile/src/components/VideoPlayer.jsx: Add a native TV overlay that shows on top of the WebView on TV. This overlay contains: a row of TVFocusable buttons for Play/Pause, Subtitle/CC toggle, Seek Back 10s, Seek Forward 10s, and Back/Exit. These buttons use injectJavaScript on the webViewRef to send commands to the embedded player (e.g., document.querySelector('video').play(), document.querySelector('video').pause(), etc).

4. In apps/mobile/src/components/VideoPlayer.jsx: Implement auto-hide for the TV overlay. Show the overlay when any D-pad key is pressed, hide it after 6 seconds of inactivity. Use a state variable (showTVControls) and a timeout ref. When showTVControls is false, the overlay is hidden (opacity 0, pointerEvents none). When true, it fades in. The first TVFocusable button (Play/Pause) should get hasTVPreferredFocus when the overlay appears.

5. In apps/mobile/src/components/VideoPlayer.jsx: Add the Back button that calls onBack() prop to navigate away from the player. Import useIsTV or use the isTV static check. Only render the TV overlay when isTV is true.

6. Ensure the overlay does NOT interfere with the WebView touch on mobile (conditionally rendered only for TV). On mobile, the existing WebView-only setup remains unchanged since it works fine with touch.
acceptance_criteria: On TV, VideoPlayer shows a native overlay with Play/Pause, Subtitle, Seek, and Back buttons
TV overlay buttons are TVFocusable and navigable via D-pad
TV overlay auto-hides after 6 seconds of inactivity
TV overlay reappears when any D-pad key is pressed
Injected JavaScript maps D-pad keys to player controls within the WebView (play/pause, seek, show controls)
On mobile, the VideoPlayer behavior is unchanged (no overlay, touch works as before)
Back button in TV overlay calls onBack to navigate away from player

findings: Implementation verified: all 28 JSX files parse OK with Babel. Studied vaplayer.ru embed source - outer page contains iframe#pf pointing to brightpathsignals.com, with postMessage forwarding between parent and inner iframe. TV overlay uses native TVFocusable buttons that inject keyboard events and postMessage commands into the WebView. Auto-hide timer at 6s with transparent focus trigger to re-show controls. lucide-react-native icons used for player buttons. The isTV static export is used in injectedJavaScript template literal (module scope) while useIsTV hook handles runtime rendering decisions.
